checks.basis: V2 HTTP transport: payment required is signalled with HTTP 402
checks.check: P1 an unpaid GET answers HTTP 402 (V2 HTTP transport)

checks.basis: V2 HTTP transport: PAYMENT-REQUIRED carries base64 JSON; V1 5.1 body
checks.check: P2 the PaymentRequired object is present and decodes (V2: base64 JSON in PAYMENT-REQUIRED; V1: JSON body)

checks.basis: The spec sets no header budget; Node fetch fails above 16 KB of headers and aiohttp near 8 KB
checks.check: P6 the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header fits common client limits (warning above 8 KB, error above 16 KB)

checks.basis: V2 5.1.2: x402Version, resource and accepts are required
checks.check: P3 PaymentRequired has x402Version, resource and a non-empty accepts[] (V2 5.1.2; V1 5.1)

checks.basis: V2 5.1.2: required accepts fields; amount in atomic token units
checks.check: P4 every accepts[] entry has the required fields with valid types (V2 5.1.2; V1 5.1)

checks.basis: EVM exact: extra.name and extra.version; SVM exact: extra.feePayer
checks.check: P5 scheme-specific extra fields are present (EVM exact: name and version; SVM exact: feePayer)

checks.basis: V2 6.1: extra.paymentFlow MUST be present when the resolved flow is not authorization (a warning: the upto SVM scheme spec allows omitting it)
checks.check: P7 an accepts[] entry whose payment flow is not authorization declares extra.paymentFlow (V2 6.1)

checks.basis: the paywall covers every method that reaches the protected handler: RFC 9110 9.3.2 HEAD is GET without the content, so an unpaid HEAD is answered 402
checks.check: R16a an unpaid HEAD on a paid route never reaches the handler: 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED like GET, or refused with 405

checks.basis: V2 HTTP transport, Error Handling: Invalid Payment (a malformed payment payload) is 400, Payment Required and Payment Failed are 402, and Server Error (500) is for the server's own failures
checks.check: R24 a malformed, non-base64 or non-object payment header gets 402 or 400 with a structured error, never a 5xx or an unhandled exception
